newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-CRICKET-Mahanama opens NZ tour account with ton.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-CRICKET-Mahanama opens NZ tour account with ton.

text.p: TAUPO, Feb 28 - Experienced Sri Lankan cricketer Roshan Mahanama opened his account in New Zealand in style on Friday with an unbeaten century against Northern Districts.

The right handed opening batsman carried his overnight score of 73 through to 106 before retiring 25 minutes before lunch on the second day of the non-first class two-day match at Owen Delaney Park, NZPA reports.
Sri Lanka went to the lunch break on 232 for four, with Hashan Tillekaratne having progressed from his overnight score of 38 to 84 while Romesh Kaluwitharana was on one.
The tourists held a first innings lead of 116 after dismissing Northern Districts for just 116 yesterday when left arm seamer Chaminda Vaas caused havoc by taking six for 22.

Mahanama, who survived a very confident caught behind appeal before scoring yesterday, was kept quiet this morning when Sri Lanka resumed on 138 for two until left arm spinner Matthew Hart was introduced to the attack 50 minutes into the session.
Mahanama showed his liking for the ex-international, depositing his first delivery straight down the ground for four before driving Hart through the covers for another boundary.
Four overs later Mahanama raised his century by forcing Hart to the fence through cover point. His 100 came up in 240 minutes, off 181 deliveries and contained 14 fours and one six.
He retired after he and Tillekaratne had put on 162 for the third wicket in 205 minutes.

Left hander Tillekaratne, who was particularly effective driving off the front foot, brought up his own half-century in the seventh over of the morning when he drove medium pacer Mark Tesar for four through mid wicket. His landmark came in 139 minutes, off 104 balls and contained seven fours.

Northern had their second success of the session when offspinner Grant Bradburn induced a false shot from Arjuna Ranatunga, who was on 11 when he leaned back to cut the ball only to hit it uppishly to Michael Parlane behind point.
